headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors: Windsurf can ingest shared files/MCP/clipboard while the prompt-list agent is untrusted docs-only content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing, docs-only agent with no isolation or I/O surfaces, so it can supply untrusted prompt text. Windsurf reads workspace files, uses clipboard and MCP, and runs a Cascade loop that can treat content as instructions. The pair creates a plausible injection path, though not a direct shared channel by default.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is copied into Windsurf prompts or files
IF Windsurf ingests workspace text or MCP output as instructions
mitigations: Review imported prompt text before use
Disable auto-execute in Windsurf
Keep prompt libraries in a read-only folder
Use a provenance tag or prefix for untrusted content
requires-engineering: add content-sanitizing import pipeline

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts touches no data classes and has network_egress none, so it is not a leakage source. Windsurf can read workspace files and send data to its model proxy/MCP servers, but the pair does not show a shared sensitive workspace or PHI/secret class. Leakage risk exists mainly if the operator places sensitive files into Windsurf and then reuses them in the prompt library.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in Windsurf and then copied into prompt assets
IF the workspace contains secrets and Windsurf uploads file contents to its backend
mitigations: Do not store secrets in the shared workspace
Use separate folders for prompts and sensitive code
Turn off clipboard-based transfer for sensitive material
Audit MCP servers before connecting them
requires-engineering: enforce workspace DLP controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts has no write or network capabilities, while Windsurf can write files, modify git state, and use a local-filesystem shared-state model. That overlap means Windsurf can mutate artifacts that the prompt-list agent may later curate or reference, creating write conflicts in default editor workflows. The uncertainty is about the exact orchestration, so severity stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local repository or prompt workspace
IF Windsurf auto-saves or commits while awesome-prompts is being updated
mitigations: Use separate working directories
Disable auto-save during curation
Avoid concurrent edits to the same git branch
Review file diffs before commit
requires-engineering: add locking around shared workspace writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt-engineering content source, so its output can become input to Windsurf without verification. Windsurf’s Cascade loop and command execution make it likely to act on that text if the operator pastes it into tasks or files. This is not high because no direct autonomous downstream action is documented, but the default workflow still permits error propagation.
conditions: IF prompt text from awesome-prompts is used as task instructions in Windsurf
IF Windsurf executes commands or edits based on unverified imported content
mitigations: Verify imported prompts before execution
Require human review for generated commands
Keep task specs separate from prompt libraries
Use test branches for prompt-driven changes
requires-engineering: add verification gates before tool use

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data class is identified for awesome-prompts, and Windsurf’s documented data classes are source code and open files. The pair therefore lacks a clear residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles. Compliance risk is limited to operator misuse if regulated data is manually introduced into Windsurf.
conditions: IF regulated data is manually opened in Windsurf
IF organizational policy forbids cloud model processing of open files
mitigations: Do not open regulated data in Windsurf
Check vendor policy before use
Separate compliant and non-compliant projects
Restrict secrets handling to approved repos
requires-engineering: configure residency-aware routing
